subject: english
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Better the devil you know than the devil you don't.

options.text: Do not trust unknown and known devils.
Being good is better with evil people.
Being cruel is better with known people.
It is easier to be in a known bad situation than being in an unknown worse situation.

solution:
The correct answer is **"It is easier to be in a known bad situation than being in an unknown worse situation."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom **"Better the devil you know than the devil you don't"** means that it is safer to deal with a familiar difficulty than to risk a new one. (किसी नई कठिनाई का जोखिम उठाने की तुलना में किसी परिचित कठिनाई से निपटना अधिक सुरक्षित है)
 
• The unknown devil may be even worse than the known one, and we may not be prepared for the challenges it brings.
 
• This idiom is often used to suggest that sticking with a current situation, even if it is not ideal, may be better than taking a risk on something new and unknown.
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.
